lessons.title: Linguistic diversity and dialects
lessons.anelcac: Notions of linguistic diversity, dialects, names of languages, geographical classification
objectives: Becoming aware of the linguistic diversity of Cameroon (about 280 languages according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas)
Distinguish language, dialect and variant according to academic definitions
Naming Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and locating it in the geographical classification of the languages of Cameroon
Adopt an attitude of respect towards all languages

teacher.intro: Lesson: Linguistic diversity and dialects. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Display the map of the Linguistic Mini-Atlas of Cameroon. Ask students which languages are spoken in their family.
**Exploration:** Have students read the definitions in the Mini-Atlas (language, dialect, patois, national language). Locate Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in its linguistic region.
**Conceptualisation:** Explain the language / dialect distinction with examples: the Bulu, Ewondo, Eton and Mangisa dialects all belong to the Beti-Fang language (Mini-Atlas).
**Application:** Complete a table: name of the language, family, main region, ISO code.
**Assessment:** Each student gives an oral presentation of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua, indicating family and region.
teacher.freedom: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.
teacher.tips: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.

student.intro: Cameroon is one of the richest nations in the world in languages — the linguistic Mini-Atlas lists about 280! In this lesson, you discover the place of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in this great family.
activities: Look at the Mini-Atlas map and find the area where Fulfulde d'Adamaoua is mainly spoken.
Copy and complete: Fulfulde d'Adamaoua belongs to the ___ family. It is mostly spoken in the ___ region.
According to the Mini-Atlas, how many living languages are there in the Fulfulde d'Adamaoua region? Note down this number.
Survey: ask an adult the name of the language in which they were raised and where it is spoken.
Memorise: **dialect** = an intelligible variant of the same language; **national language** = language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State (ACA LAN).
student.memo: Cameroon has about **280 languages** according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas. Fulfulde d'Adamaoua belongs to a Cameroonian language family and has its own dialectal variants. According to the ACA LAN, a national language is the language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State.

lessons.title: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas
lessons.anelcac: Classification of the languages of Cameroon: linguistic areas, families, ALCAM atlas
objectives: Name the main linguistic areas of Cameroon
Read and interpret an extract from a linguistic atlas (ALCAM / Mini-Atlas)
Classify Fulfulde d'Adamaoua according to its typological criteria
Producing a short text presenting Fulfulde d'Adamaoua

teacher.intro: Lesson: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Go back over the definitions. How many language families do students remember?
**Presentation:** The 8 world language families according to Ethnologue (Niger-Kordofanian, Nilo-Saharan, Afro-Asiatic…). Place Cameroonian languages within this whole.
**Explanation:** Show how to find Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in the ALCAM: ISO code, family, location.
**Guided practice:** In pairs, students find 3 languages neighbouring Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and note their ISO codes.
**Production:** 5-line paragraph presenting Fulfulde d'Adamaoua (family, region, speakers, distinctive feature).
teacher.freedom: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.
teacher.tips: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.

student.intro: A linguistic atlas is a specialised map. The ALCAM (Atlas of the Languages of Cameroon) and the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas let you locate Fulfulde d'Adamaoua precisely.
activities: On the Mini-Atlas map, locate Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and note its administrative region.
List 3 languages whose area is adjacent to that of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
Classify these 4 languages in a table: Language | Family | Main region.
Write an introductory paragraph about Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with at least 5 pieces of information taken from the atlas.
Memorise: **ISO 639** = international language codes; **ALCAM** = Atlas des Langues du Cameroun.
student.memo: The **ALCAM** and the **LACAGEO Mini-Atlas** list and locate all the national languages of Cameroon. Cameroon has 8 main language families. Fulfulde d'Adamaoua appears there with its family and its location. Knowing how to read a linguistic atlas is reading the history of peoples.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Vowels of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
lessons.anelcac: AGLC vowels — simple, specific, complex
objectives: Identify the simple vowels of the phonological system of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Recognising specific vowels absent from French
Pronouncing vowels correctly in the context of a word
Transcribing words containing vowels according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Fulfulde d'Adamaoua vowels. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write known words in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua on the board and ask which sounds students hear.
**Presentation:** Introduce the AGLC. Write the simple vowels of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua on the board, articulating them clearly.
**Explanation:** Vowels specific to Fulfulde d'Adamaoua that are absent from French (nasal, particular openness…). Listening and repetition exercises.
**Application:** List of 10 words — students underline the vowels and indicate: simple or specific.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 simple words — students transcribe them with the correct vowels.
teacher.freedom: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.
teacher.tips: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.

student.intro: Every language has its own sounds. In Fulfulde d'Adamaoua, some vowels do not exist in French. This lesson teaches you to hear, pronounce and write them.
activities: Listen to the recordings of the Fulfulde d'Adamaoua vocabulary and identify the vowels you hear.
Classify the vowels: **Shared with French** | **Specific to Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**.
Transcribe the 5 dictated words, taking care to note each vowel correctly.
Find 3 words in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua for each specific vowel and write them down.
Memorise: **AGLC** = Alphabet Général des Langues Camerounaises, the official reference.
student.memo: The vowel system of **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** includes simple vowels and specific vowels (e.g. nasalised vowels). They are written using the **AGLC**. Mastery of vowels is the basis of reading and writing in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Fulfulde d'Adamaoua consonants and written production
lessons.anelcac: Consonants — simple, specific, complex; written production of vowels and consonants
objectives: Identify the consonant system of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Recognising specific consonants absent from French
Articulate consonants correctly in context
Writing words with vowels and consonants correctly notated

teacher.intro: Lesson: Fulfulde d'Adamaoua consonants and written production. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the vowels. What is a consonant?
**Presentation:** Table of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua consonants according to the AGLC. Stress the specific consonants (labio-velars, prenasalised, implosives…).
**Explanation:** Articulating difficult consonants: in isolation → syllable → word.
**Application:** Minimal pairs: listening to words that differ only by one consonant.
**Production:** 5 simple sentences in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with careful consonant transcription.
teacher.freedom: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.
teacher.tips: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.

student.intro: After the vowels, here are the consonants of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua! Some are unique — you will only hear them in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and in a few neighbouring African languages.
activities: Listen to the minimal pairs and tick the word you hear (e.g. bìlí / pìlí).
Transcribe 5 dictated words, paying attention to the specific consonants.
Find in the vocabulary all the words containing a prenasalised consonant. How many do you find?
Compose 3 simple sentences in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua, each with at least one specific consonant.
Memorise: **minimal pair** = two words identical except for one phoneme.
student.memo: The consonant system of **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** includes consonants shared with French and specific consonants (implosives, prenasalised, labio-velars…). Writing them according to the **AGLC** is essential for reading and writing.

lessons.title: Definition and functions of tones
lessons.anelcac: Tones — definition, function, presentation; simple tones (high, low, mid)
objectives: Define tone as a distinctive feature of tone languages
Distinguish lexical tone from grammatical tone
Identify the simple tones of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Transcribing words with their tones according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Definition and function of tones. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Say two Fulfulde d'Adamaoua words that are written the same but have different tones and different meanings.
**Presentation:** Define tone. Present the simple tones of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and their AGLC diacritics.
**Explanation:** Simple tones: high (´), low (`), mid (¯). Have students repeat each tone.
**Application:** Match recorded words with their tone notation.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 words — students note the tones.
teacher.freedom: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.
teacher.tips: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.

student.intro: Fulfulde d'Adamaoua is a tonal language: the pitch of your voice changes the meaning of the word! You will learn to hear and write down these tones.
activities: Listen to the pairs of words. For each pair, are the tones the same or different?
Transcribe 5 words with their tones using the AGLC diacritics (´ ` ¯).
Find 2 words in the vocabulary that differ only in tone. What does each one mean?
Sing the tones of a 3-syllable word as High-Low-High, then Low-High-Low. What difference do you hear?
Memorise: high tone = ´ ; low tone = ` ; mid tone = ¯.
student.memo: In **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**, tone is phonological: it distinguishes words with different meanings. The **simple tones** are high (´), low (`), and sometimes mid (¯). They are written using the **AGLC** diacritics.

lessons.title: Complex tones and tone-marked written production
lessons.anelcac: Complex tones (rising, falling); finding the tone of a word; tonal written production
objectives: Identify the complex tones of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua (rising, falling)
Finding the tone of a word by the isolation method
Transcribing sentences with full tone marking
Producing a short text in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with correct tones

teacher.intro: Lesson: Complex tones and tonal written production. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the simple tones. Announce that some syllables carry two tones in succession.
**Presentation:** Complex tones: falling (̂), rising (̌). Let students hear them and reproduce them.
**Explanation:** Isolation method: say the word with an artificial high tone, then a low one, and listen to which sounds natural.
**Application:** Students find the tone of 10 words in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua using the isolation method.
**Production:** Dialogue of 6 lines in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with complete tone notation.
teacher.freedom: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.
teacher.tips: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.

student.intro: You know the simple tones. Now for the complex tones of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua — syllables that rise and fall at the same time!
activities: Listen to the recorded words and sort them: Simple tone | Complex tone.
Apply the isolation method to 5 words: say them high, then low, and note the tone you perceive.
Transcribe a dialogue of 4 lines in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with all the tones marked.
Write a 3-sentence text in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua about an action from your daily life, with tone marking.
Memorise: falling tone = ̂ ; rising tone = ̌.
student.memo: The **complex tones** of **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** (falling ̂, rising ̌) are melodic movements on a single syllable. The **isolation method** makes it possible to find the tone of an unknown word. A transcription in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua without tones is incomplete.

lessons.title: The noun base and noun classes
lessons.anelcac: NP: constituents, base noun + affixes, noun classes, personal pronouns
objectives: Identify the structure of the noun in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua (base + affixes)
Recognising the noun classes of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Form the singular and plural of nouns
Use the personal pronouns corresponding to noun classes

teacher.intro: Lesson: The noun base and noun classes. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a noun in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in the singular and plural. What changes?
**Presentation:** Noun class: in Bantu and Bantoid languages, nouns are grouped into classes marked by prefixes.
**Explanation:** Main noun classes of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with singular and plural prefixes.
**Application:** Table: singular → plural for 10 nouns.
**Assessment:** Identify the noun class of 5 nouns.
teacher.freedom: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).
teacher.tips: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).

student.intro: In Fulfulde d'Adamaoua, nouns are organised into **classes**. Each class has its own prefixes for the singular and plural — a much richer system than gender in French!
activities: Using the Fulfulde d'Adamaoua vocabulary, make a table: Singular | Plural | Noun class.
Identify the class prefix in each noun. Highlight it.
Put the following 5 nouns into the plural by changing the prefix according to the class.
Match each noun with its corresponding class pronoun.
Memorise: **noun class** = grammatical category of nouns, marked by prefixes.
student.memo: In **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**, nouns are organised into **noun classes** marked by prefixes. A change of prefix indicates number. Pronouns, adjectives and verbs agree with the class of the noun.

lessons.title: Noun determiners
lessons.anelcac: Determiners: possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives; noun class agreement
objectives: Identify the different types of determiners in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Make determiners agree with the noun according to the noun class
Build complex noun phrases
Producing sentences with complete NPs

teacher.intro: Lesson: Noun determiners. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a simple noun phrase. How can it be enriched?
**Presentation:** Determiners in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives.
**Explanation:** Each determiner agrees with the class of the noun (same class prefix or suffix).
**Application:** Complete noun phrases with the correct determiner according to the class.
**Production:** 5 complex noun phrases (noun + 2 determiners) used in sentences.
teacher.freedom: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua compared with French.
teacher.tips: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua compared with French.

student.intro: A noun with its determiners becomes much more precise! In Fulfulde d'Adamaoua, determiners agree with the **noun class**.
activities: Complete the NPs with the correct possessive determiner according to the noun class.
Underline the determiners in 5 sentences in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and identify their type.
Turn each simple noun phrase into a complex noun phrase by adding a demonstrative and a numeral.
Write 5 sentences in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with at least two determiners per noun phrase.
Memorise: **class agreement** = the determiner changes form according to the noun class.
student.memo: In **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**, all determiners (possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives) agree with the **noun class** of the noun. A **complex NP** = noun + nominal base + agreeing determiners.

lessons.title: The verb stem and conjugation
lessons.anelcac: VP: constituents, stem, affixes, conjugation, verb tenses
objectives: Identify the verb stem and the conjugation affixes in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Conjugate a verb in the main tenses
Analyse the morphological structure of a verb form
Use verb forms correctly in sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The verb stem and conjugation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a verb form in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and ask students to identify the stem.
**Presentation:** Break down a verb form: subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes.
**Explanation:** Conjugation paradigm of a common verb in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in several tenses.
**Application:** Conjugation table: 3 common verbs.
**Assessment:** Translate 5 sentences from French into Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
teacher.freedom: The TAM system of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.
teacher.tips: The TAM system of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.

student.intro: The verb is the heart of the sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. It alone carries tense, aspect, mood and subject! In this lesson, you take apart the verbal mechanics.
activities: Break down 5 verb forms in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: subject prefix | TAM marker | stem | suffix.
Conjugate the verb 'to eat' in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in 3 different tenses for all persons.
Identify the tense of 5 sentences in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua and justify your answer.
Translate 3 sentences from French into Fulfulde d'Adamaoua, taking care with the conjugation.
Memorise: **TAM** = Tense-Aspect-Mood; this is what verbal affixes express in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
student.memo: In **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**, a verb form = subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes. The **TAM** (Tense-Aspect-Mood) system expresses more precise temporal and aspectual nuances than in French.

lessons.title: Verbal moods and negation
lessons.anelcac: Moods: indicative, imperative; negation; written production of simple/complex VP
objectives: Identify and use the main verbal moods of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Form the verbal negation
Build simple and complex verb phrases
Producing a text with a variety of moods and aspects

teacher.intro: Lesson: Verbal moods and negation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Give an order in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Which mood is used?
**Presentation:** Moods in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: indicative, imperative, and other aspectual moods.
**Explanation:** Formation of the negative in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: prefix, negative suffix, or particle.
**Application:** Turn 5 affirmative sentences into negative ones and vice versa.
**Production:** 8-sentence text alternating affirmation, negation and imperative.
teacher.freedom: Negation in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.
teacher.tips: Negation in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.

student.intro: Giving an order, expressing doubt, denying an action — each nuance has its own form in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua!
activities: Put the 5 given sentences into the negative form.
Turn these 5 statements into imperatives addressed to a friend.
Identify the mood and polarity (affirmative/negative) of each sentence in the text provided.
Write a dialogue of 6 lines including at least 2 imperatives and 2 negations.
Memorise: **mood** = the way of viewing the action; **negation** = grammatical marker denying the action.
student.memo: In **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**, the main moods are the **indicative** and the **imperative**. **Negation** is marked by a particle or a specific affix. The diversity of moods is an expressive richness of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
lessons.title: The simple sentence and its types
lessons.anelcac: Simple, interrogative, negative and imperative sentence; word order
objectives: Analyse the structure of the simple sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Distinguish the 4 types of sentences
Mastering the order of constituents
Producing varied simple sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The simple sentence and its types. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Who does what?
**Presentation:** Basic constituent order in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Compare with French.
**Explanation:** The 4 sentence types from the same basic sentence.
**Application:** Turn declarative sentences into interrogative ones, then into negative ones.
**Production:** 8 varied sentences (2 per type) about school life.
teacher.freedom: Word order in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.
teacher.tips: Word order in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.

student.intro: A well-constructed sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua follows precise rules. You learn the types of sentences and word order.
activities: Identify the order of constituents in 5 sentences in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
Turn 4 declarative sentences into yes/no questions.
Turn these 4 sentences into negatives.
Write 2 sentences of each type (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative).
Memorise: the basic order in **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** is typologically stable.
student.memo: The **simple sentence** in **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** has a characteristic order of constituents. The 4 types (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative) are formed with specific grammatical markers.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
lessons.title: Logical connectors and the complex sentence
lessons.anelcac: Logical connectors, complex sentence, coordination, subordination; written production
objectives: Identify the logical connectors of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Distinguish coordination from subordination
Build complex sentences
Producing a coherent text with syntactic variety

teacher.intro: Lesson: Logical connectors and the complex sentence. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a short story in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Which words link the sentences?
**Presentation:** Connectors in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
**Explanation:** Complex sentence by coordination / by subordination. Examples in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
**Application:** Link 5 pairs of simple sentences with the appropriate connector.
**Production:** 10-sentence text on 'A day in my village' with 5 different connectors.
teacher.freedom: The connectors of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.
teacher.tips: The connectors of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.

student.intro: To tell stories and argue, you need to link your sentences. The **logical connectors** of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua are your tools!
activities: Underline all the connectors in the text provided.
Classify them: Addition | Cause | Consequence | Opposition | Time.
Link 5 pairs of sentences with the most appropriate connector.
Write a text of 8 sentences with at least 4 different connectors.
Memorise: coordination = same level; subordination = one sentence inside another.
student.memo: In **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua**, **logical connectors** make it possible to build coherent **complex sentences**. Varying syntactic structures improves the quality of written and spoken expression.

lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
lessons.anelcac: Everyday communication situations: greetings, introductions, polite expressions
objectives: Mastering greeting formulas according to context
Introducing yourself and someone else in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Use polite and respectful expressions
Holding a short everyday conversation

teacher.intro: Lesson: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Two students meet at the market. Act out the scene in French, then ask how to say it in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
**Presentation:** Greetings in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua according to the time of day, age and context.
**Explanation:** Formulas of respect towards elders, specific to Fulfulde d'Adamaoua culture.
**Role play:** In groups of 2, simulate encounters in various contexts (market, school, ceremony).
**Production:** Dialogue of 10 lines between two people of different generations.
teacher.freedom: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.
teacher.tips: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.

student.intro: Knowing how to greet in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua means respecting the culture! The greetings change depending on whom you greet and at what time.
activities: Complete the table of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua greetings: Time | Formula | Expected response.
Play role A: greeting an elder at the morning market.
Make up a dialogue of 8 lines between a child and their grandfather.
Note down 3 Fulfulde d'Adamaoua politeness formulas with no direct equivalent in French.
Memorise the morning and evening greeting formulas, and those for elders, in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
student.memo: **Greetings** in **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** vary according to the time of day, status and social context. They reflect the community's values of respect and solidarity.

lessons.title: Express everyday needs and actions
lessons.anelcac: Real-life situations: shopping, requests for help, travelling, daily activities
objectives: Express everyday needs in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Describe daily activities
Use vocabulary for places and actions of everyday life
Producing a descriptive text on a typical day

teacher.intro: Lesson: Expressing everyday needs and actions. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Images of scenes from daily life — market, field, school, home. How can they be described in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua?
**Presentation:** Thematic vocabulary: food, travel, household activities.
**Simulation:** Market scene: buyer and seller in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
**Application:** Describe your day in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua (from waking up to going to bed).
**Production:** 10-sentence text: 'My day in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua'.
teacher.freedom: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.
teacher.tips: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.

student.intro: You know how to greet people. Now you are going to manage in everyday situations in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: at the market, on the road, at home.
activities: Match each picture of a scene from daily life with the corresponding word or sentence in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
Play the role of the seller at the market: answer the requests in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
Write 5 sentences describing your morning activities from the time you wake up.
Translate these 5 sentences about daily journeys into Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
Memorise 10 everyday words in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with their French translation.
student.memo: The **everyday** vocabulary in **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** covers food, getting around and household activities. Mastering it allows functional communication in all contexts.

lessons.title: Argue and persuade in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
lessons.anelcac: Elaborate communication: argumentation, narration, formal speech
objectives: Build a simple argument in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Use the expressions of formal speech
Narrating a past event coherently
Delivering a 2-minute oral speech in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua

teacher.intro: Lesson: Arguing and persuading in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a proverb in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua. Ask students to explain it and defend it.
**Presentation:** Formulas of formal oral speech in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua: forms of address, opening, closing.
**Explanation:** Structure of an argument: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion.
**Practice:** Debate: for or against the use of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua at school? Each group defends its position.
**Production:** 2-minute speech on a given theme.
teacher.freedom: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.
teacher.tips: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.

student.intro: In Fulfulde d'Adamaoua cultures, well-spoken words are a force. You learn to argue and persuade with eloquence.
activities: Identify in the text: thesis, arguments, examples.
Prepare 3 arguments to defend the teaching of Fulfulde d'Adamaoua in primary school.
Give an opening speech for a ceremony in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
Narration: tell in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua about a memorable event from your school life.
Memorise the opening and closing formulas of a formal speech in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
student.memo: **Argumentation** in **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** follows this pattern: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion. **Formal speech** follows precise cultural conventions. Mastery of elaborate oral expression is a high-level skill.

lessons.title: Oral literature and advanced written production
lessons.anelcac: Oral literature: proverbs, tales, riddles; long written production
objectives: Analyse the structure of a tale or a riddle in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua
Identify the themes and values conveyed
Writing a short tale following the conventions of the genre
Using oral literature as a teaching resource

teacher.intro: Lesson: Oral literature and advanced written production. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Tell or play a short tale in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua.
**Presentation:** Genres of oral literature: tales, proverbs, riddles, epics.
**Analysis:** Structure of the tale: initial situation → disruption → events → resolution → moral.
**Application:** Analyse a tale provided, following this structure.
**Production:** Tale of at least 15 lines in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with an explicit moral.
teacher.freedom: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.
teacher.tips: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.

student.intro: Fulfulde d'Adamaoua tales, proverbs and riddles are literary works in their own right. You will analyse them and you will create your own!
activities: Read the tale provided and identify the 5 stages of its narrative structure.
Identify 3 moral values taught by this tale.
Translate a proverb in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua into French and explain its figurative meaning.
Write a short tale (15 lines) in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua with a moral about work or respect.
Memorise: tale = fictional narrative with an educational purpose; proverb = brief formula of collective wisdom.
student.memo: The **oral literature** of **Fulfulde d'Adamaoua** (tales, proverbs, riddles) transmits the values of the community. The tale has a 5-stage structure. Writing it in Fulfulde d'Adamaoua draws on all the language skills acquired.

lessons.title: Who are the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga)? Identity, language and territory
lessons.anelcac: Cultural areas, cultural identity, settlement
objectives: Name the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) community and explain its name
Locating your territory and its neighbours
Telling one's origin according to tradition
lessons.competence: Introduce the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.
lessons.situation: A pen pal from another region asks you to introduce the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) community to them: who are they, where do they live, where did they come from?
lessons.materiel: Map of Cameroon, cultural profile of the community (“Cultures” section of Likalo).

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Present the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “A pen friend from another region asks you to introduce the Fulani Walarbe community (Gashiga): who are they, where do they live, where do they come from?” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What do the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) call themselves and what does this name mean? — What language do they speak, and where else is it spoken? — Which peoples do they live with? — Where did they come from, according to tradition?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Majority group, integrated with the Fali and the Bata, who widely speak Fulfulde. • Fulfulde is the great language of the North, the Far North and Adamawa. • One may marry anyone of another ethnic group, provided the religion is the same; formerly, people married only within the group. • The lands were acquired gradually, through neighbourliness and marriage alliances. • Origin: Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger; Cameroonian stages at Bashéo, Demsa and in the Mandara mountains. Ties with these places are maintained.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The Fulani Walarbe of Gashiga, the majority in their area, live alongside the Fali and the Bata. Coming from Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger via Bashéo, Demsa and the Mandara Mountains, they form a hereditary lamidat where Islam governs social life; livestock rearing, farming, trade and Koranic teaching are its pillars.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: On a map of Cameroon, locate the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) community and its neighbours, then write 5 sentences to introduce it to your pen pal.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.intro: Discover the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) community: its name, its language, its neighbours and its history.

activities.title: I locate
activities.instruction: On a map, place the community, its region and its neighbours.

activities.title: I trace the history
activities.instruction: On a timeline or a map, draw the migration route told in tradition.

activities.title: I compare
activities.instruction: Compare the origin of this people with that of your own community: 2 similarities, 2 differences.

student.memo: The Fulani Walarbe of Gashiga, the majority in their area, live alongside the Fali and the Bata. Coming from Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger via Bashéo, Demsa and the Mandara Mountains, they form a hereditary lamidat where Islam governs social life; livestock rearing, farming, trade and Koranic teaching are its pillars.

lessons.title: Power and social organisation among the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga)
lessons.anelcac: Socio-political organisation, rules for living together
objectives: Identify traditional authorities
Explain how decisions are made
Identifying the rules of deference
lessons.competence: Describe how the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.
lessons.situation: An important decision has to be made for the whole Fulani Walarbe village (Gashiga). Who decides, and how?
lessons.materiel: The community's cultural profile, paper and felt-tip pens for the organisation chart.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe how the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “An important decision has to be made for the whole village of the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga). Who decides, and how?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — Who holds authority? — How are decisions made (consensus, vote, the chief's decision)? — What rules of respect and deference are observed? — Which groups or societies play a particular role?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • A lamido, whose throne is passed on by inheritance, leads the group; an alkali (judge) dispenses justice in the lamidat. • Men and women live separately; the man provides for the woman, who does not go out without permission. • Women do not look men in the eyes. Relations with neighbours are not always harmonious.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: A lamido, whose throne is passed down by inheritance, leads the group; an alkali (judge) dispenses justice in the lamidat. Men and women live separately; the man provides for the woman's needs, and she does not go out without permission. Women do not look men in the eyes. Relations with neighbours are not always harmonious.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Draw a diagram (organisation chart) of power among the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga), then explain in 3 sentences how a decision is made.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.anelcac: Ways of life: culinary practices
objectives: Naming traditional foods and drinks

lessons.competence: Identify the traditional dishes and drinks of the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga), describe how they are prepared and bring out their cultural significance.
lessons.situation: Your class is preparing a food fair. Your group must present a traditional dish of the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga).

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Identify the traditional dishes and drinks of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), describe how they are prepared and draw out their cultural significance.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “Your class is preparing a food fair. Your group must present a traditional dish of the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga).” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the main dishes and drinks? — What products are they made from? Where do these products come from? — Who prepares them, and on what occasions? — What do they say about the community's living environment?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Traditional dishes: millet and maize, baobab leaves, curdled and fresh milk, biradam, lindirmou. • Drinks: milk. • Men: livestock rearing (cattle, sheep, goats) for sale, farming, trade, Koranic teaching. Women: embroidery and beadwork crafts, Koranic teaching.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga) eat mainly millet and maize, baobab leaves, curdled and fresh milk, biradam. Traditional drinks: milk. These dishes are linked to the group's activities and to the products of its environment.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Choose a dish of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga): write its sheet (name in the language, ingredients, steps, occasion when it is served).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

lessons.anelcac: Ways of life: clothing practices, crafts
objectives: Describe traditional clothing
Identify craft objects and their use
Explain the criteria of beauty
lessons.competence: Describe the clothing, adornments and craft objects of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), and explain their use and value.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — How did people dress in the past, and how do they dress today? — Do clothes indicate status or occasion? — What objects are made, from what materials, and for what uses? — What are the criteria of beauty?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following elements: • Boubous for men, wrappers for women. • Men: livestock (cattle, sheep, goats) for sale, crops, trade, Koranic teaching. lessons.title: Birth, name and the passage to adulthood among the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga)
lessons.anelcac: Key events: birth, naming, initiation
objectives: Explain the meaning of a birth
Describe how names are given
Describe the passage to adulthood
lessons.competence: Explain how the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga) welcome a child, give them a name and mark their entry into adulthood.
lessons.situation: A child has just been born into a Fulani Walarbe family (Gashiga). How will the child be named, and how will they become an adult?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain how the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) welcome a child, give them a name and mark their entry into adulthood.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “A child has just been born into a Fulani Walarbe family (Gashiga). How will the child be named, and how will they become an adult?” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What does a birth mean for the community? — Who gives the name, when and how? — Can the name change during a lifetime? — When and how does one become a man or a woman?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-IV — Cultural practices in communities (Level I)
lessons.title: Leisure: traditional music and dances of the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: leisure, traditional dances
objectives: Identify dances and their occasions
Describe a dance and its instruments
Perform the dance

vocabulary.langText: danses du Ramadan et de la Tabaski
danse de la fête du lamido

lessons.competence: Identify the traditional dances of the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga), choose the most representative one, describe it, bring out its cultural significance and act it out.
lessons.situation: Taking part in cultural life in the family and in society: the class prepares a Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) dance performance for the cultural day.
lessons.materiel: Instruments or recordings, costumes, clear space.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Identify the traditional dances of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), choose the most representative one, describe it, draw out its cultural significance and act it out.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “Participation in cultural life in the family and in society: the class is preparing a Fulani Walarbe dance performance (Gashiga) for the cultural day.” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — Which dances are practised, and on what occasions? — Who dances (men, women, children, initiates)? When and where? — Which instruments, songs and outfits are used? — What is the cultural meaning of the chosen dance?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • Rhythms: wadou'el, sorol, dat'do, dogoulayel; instruments: tam-tam, horns, griots' songs. • People dance during Ramadan, Tabaski and the lamido's festival, which brings together all the ethnic groups in front of the palace.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Among the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), the traditional dances (Ramadan and Tabaski dances, dance of the lamido's festival) accompany the major moments of life: festivals, mourning, weddings, initiations. Instruments: tam-tam, horns, griots. Festival(s): Ramadan, Tabaski.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Describe a dance of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) (participants, time, instruments, gestures, meaning), then perform it with your group.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.intro: Discover the music and dances of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), then learn to perform one.

activities.title: I understand
activities.instruction: Explain whether it is a dance of joy, mourning, initiation or war.

activities.title: I practise
activities.instruction: With your group, act out the dance in front of the class.

student.memo: Among the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), the traditional dances (Ramadan and Tabaski dances, dance of the lamido's festival) accompany the major moments of life: festivals, mourning, weddings, initiations. Instruments: tam-tam, horns, griots. Festival(s): Ramadan, Tabaski.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-IV — Cultural practices in communities (Level I)
lessons.title: Traditional economy and access to land among the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: traditional economy
objectives: Identify economic activities
Explain the division of tasks
Explain access to land
lessons.competence: Describe the economic activities of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.
lessons.situation: A development project wants to help the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga). First you need to understand how they work and who owns the land.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe the economic activities of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A development project wants to help the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga). First, we need to understand how they work and who owns the land.” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the activities of men? of women? — Who owns the land and how is it accessed? — Which products are sold or exchanged? — Have these activities changed?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Men: livestock (cattle, sheep, goats) for sale, farming, trade, Quranic teaching. Women: embroidery and bead crafts, Quranic teaching. • The land, at first belonging to no one, was appropriated by the monarchy and belongs to the lamidat. • Crafts: cotton weaving, embroidery of boubous, basketry, leatherwork (shoes, clothing, mats, djangardé cloth).

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Men: livestock rearing (cattle, sheep, goats) for sale, farming, trade, Koranic teaching. Women: embroidery and beadwork crafts, Koranic teaching. Land, at first owned by no one, was appropriated by the monarchy and belongs to the lamidat.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Make a two-column table (men / women) of the activities of the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga), then explain how land is accessed.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Beliefs, sacred places and taboos among the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: symbolism, rites, taboos
objectives: Explain beliefs about life and death
Identify sacred places
Explain the role of taboos
lessons.competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga), and their role in regulating social life.
lessons.situation: A visitor arrives among the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga). Which places and rules must they absolutely respect?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga), and their role in regulating social life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A visitor arrives among the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga). What places and rules must they absolutely respect?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the beliefs about birth and death? — Which places are sacred, and why? — What are the main taboos, and for whom? — How were serious offences atoned for?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present, or have the students discover, the following: • No ancestor cult: religious life is Islamic. • Symbolic places: Mount Tenguelin, refuge of the Fali during the jihad, and the villages of Pomla Petel, Chakare (“the middle”) and Pomla Manga. • Birth is a blessing that perpetuates the parent; death is the return to God, and prayers are said for the rest of the deceased. • Prohibitions: for the man, alcohol, games of chance, crime; for the woman, disrespect towards her husband and going out without permission; for the child, theft and disrespect towards elders. • Serious offences: crime, adultery, alcohol, hypocrisy, dishonouring one's parents, severely punished.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: No ancestor cult: religious life is Islamic. Symbolic places: Mount Tenguelin, refuge of the Fali during the jihad, and the villages of Pomla Petel, Chakare (“the middle”) and Pomla Manga.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Write a short guide to good conduct for a visitor among the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) (3 places or rules to respect, with the reason for each).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.memo: No ancestor cult: religious life is Islamic. Symbolic places: Mount Tenguelin, refuge of the Fali during the jihad, and the villages of Pomla Petel, Chakare (“the middle”) and Pomla Manga.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and counting in Fulfulde
lessons.anelcac: Traditional media and transmission: everyday language
objectives: Greeting according to the time of day
Introducing yourself
Counting from 1 to 10

vocabulary.frenchText: morning greetings (as a sign of deference/respect)

lessons.competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Fulani Walarbe (Gashiga) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.
lessons.situation: You are visiting a Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga) family. Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in sharing the kola nuts while counting.
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile (“Common expressions” and “Counting” sections), kola nuts or small objects.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Peuls Walarbe (Gashiga) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “You are visiting a Fulani Walarbe family (Gashiga). Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in the sharing of the kola nuts by counting.” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — How do you greet people depending on the time of day? — How do you introduce yourself (name, origin, place of residence)? — How do you count from 1 to 10? Is the system decimal, vigesimal…? — Why is language a tool of transmission?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • The language of the community is Fulfulde. • Greeting formulas: Mi hofni = Hello (neutral formula, at any time); A wali djamna = morning greeting (one person); One wali djamna = morning greeting (several people). • Counting from 1 to 5: Gotel, Didi, Tati, Naye, Djaye. • Appellatives: walarbé, djasi, batoudi, bouré.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Greeting and counting in Fulfulde are the first steps towards communicating with the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga). Polite expressions show the respect owed to people according to the time of day and their rank.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Role play in pairs: greet each other, introduce yourselves, ask where the other person comes from and count objects from 1 to 10.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.intro: Learn to greet, introduce yourself and count in Fulfulde.

activities.title: I greet

activities.title: I count

activities.title: I pass on

student.memo: Greeting and counting in Fulfulde are the first steps towards communicating with the Walarbe Fulani (Gashiga). Polite expressions show the respect owed to people according to the time of day and their rank.
